description:
memory.rs:198-214 — recompute_calendars_with_events scans every CalendarEvent in the account on every CalendarEvent create/update/destroy AND every seed_object('CalendarEvent', ...). The scan clones the entire event map (line 202: .cloned()) and rebuilds the calendars_with_events HashSet from scratch.

Complexity at N events:
- Each create: O(N) (the scan) + O(1) (the actual insert).
- Total ingest of N events: O(N²).
- Plus an O(N) clone on every operation.

The fix is straightforward: on create_object, parse the new event's calendarIds and union it into calendars_with_events. On destroy, only recompute if the destroyed event was the LAST event in some calendar (cheap check: scan the remaining events only when needed). On update, diff the before/after calendarIds. None of this needs the full-scan + clone.

This is a reference impl so absolute speed is not the goal, but workspace AGENTS.md says MemoryBackend should be 'documented, complete, source-readable implementation of the CalendarsBackend trait to study when writing a real (database-backed) backend' (memory.rs:9-11). A downstream contributor who reads recompute_calendars_with_events and copies the pattern into a SQL backend will produce a backend that materializes 'every event in the account' on every mutation. Persisting that pattern is bad.

Workspace integration tests use small fixtures (≤10 events) so the O(N²) ingest never manifests in CI runtime, but a smoke test that seeds 1000 events would take noticeably longer than necessary.

P2 efficiency, not P0/P1, because it does not affect correctness and the integration-test scale never hits it. Worth fixing because the pattern is teach-by-example and the cost grows with consumer adoption.

Cookie-cutter consideration: check if contacts/chat/tasks/filenode siblings have similar full-rescan patterns. If so this is a workspace-sweep candidate; canonical fix lands first in mail-server (mail-server already has different shape so no direct sibling here).
title: recompute_calendars_with_events is O(N) per mutation; quadratic ingest
